title: The Value of Platform Endorsement
authors: Mimansa Bairathi; Xu Zhang; Anja Lambrecht
eligible_reason: Randomized experiment on platform endorsement: user-level Poisson regressions of impressions, clicks and orders on the treatment-group indicator with week-of-first-visit and category FE and past-orders control (ITT and propensity-weighted ATT). Treatment is randomly assigned at the user level, not staggered; models are nonlinear.
design_notes: MainEffect.do (CRLF line endings, hence the sparse inventory): Table 5 glm/poisson tot_orders i.group total_orders_lifetime i.week ibn.cat_idf [pw=psweights1], vce(cluster userid); Tables 7-12 add heterogeneity interactions (group x around, similar_price, orders_2weeks, prof_buyer, second_exposure). Descriptives.R produces Tables 1, 2, 4, 6.
data_files_note: README.rtf: proprietary data under NDA; shipped data are a random 50% of users with random noise added to each variable and hashed identifiers; results differ from the paper.
data_provenance_note: 50% user subsample plus observation-level noise and hashed IDs.
software_notes: Stata (glm/poisson, esttab) and R for descriptives.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text and papers/ checked Nov 2); the OpenAlex abstract in data/frame/mksc.jsonl is a one-sentence summary. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
